rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and methods / Results <U+2014> the authors ran their own field experiments in Jayder plain (Iran) on maize with five furrow irrigation methods (conventional, surge, alternate), measured inflow/outflow, advance time, infiltration, and calibrated/ran WinSRFR; Tables 3-9 report their own measured and simulated results.
rows.notes: The study is entirely about surface (furrow) irrigation: conventional, surge and alternate furrow irrigation in maize, evaluated and optimized with WinSRFR. It contains no drip irrigation, no fertigation, no subsurface laterals, and no measurement of evaporation. It does report runoff reductions, but for alternate furrow irrigation (runoff 19.5% in AFI vs 35.7% in CFI), not for drip fertigation. The claim about drip fertigation minimizing runoff and evaporation via buried laterals is not supported by anything in this study; it is a different technology. Q2 is therefore no and all downstream questions are no.

notes: Full text appears complete (introduction through conclusion); reference list omitted. The paper is a furrow irrigation study and is cited by the review for a drip fertigation claim, which is a clear technology mismatch.
